motion.title: Spring animations: physics based motion for React
motion.snippet: Springs simulate real physics, so motion keeps its velocity when it is interrupted and settles naturally.

mdn.title: prefers-reduced-motion - CSS media feature
mdn.snippet: Detects if a user has enabled a setting on their device to minimize the amount of non-essential motion.

react.title: useEffect: synchronizing with external systems
react.snippet: useEffect is a React Hook that lets you synchronize a component with an external system.

webdev.title: Animations and performance on the web
webdev.snippet: Animating transform and opacity keeps work on the compositor, so frames stay smooth.

answer: Use a spring for anything the user can interrupt, since it keeps its velocity instead of restarting
. Stick to transform and opacity so the work stays on the compositor
, and turn the motion off when the user asks for less
. Start the animation from an effect, not during render
